gap: No result ChatGPT got says how long the Anker Prime 100W 3-Port (A2688) can hold its rated 100 W. Techtest.org measured about one hour at 100 W before it overheated and throttled, with efficiency between 86.6 % and 91.1 %.
standout_why: I compared against the A2688 page (results 2 and 7), the A120F page (results 1, 3 and 4) and the Anker blog 'Laptop Charger Pro Review' (result 11, dated 2026-09-22). The A2688 page gives only rated per-port splits (100 W from one port, 89 W across three) and the claim that ActiveShield 2.0 checks temperature 3 million times a day. It has no measured temperature, efficiency or sustained-output figure. The A120F page and the Anker blog cover a different model, the A120F single-port charger. Their numbers are Anker's own claims: holds 100 W at 25 °C, surface temperature up to 10 °C lower, 0–50 % in 30 minutes. The blog says only that 'plenty of adapters taper to 65W' and names no product. None of the 12 results gives an independent measurement of any charger ChatGPT recommended.
decides: This supports the Anker Prime 100W for a laptop that draws close to 100 W for less than an hour. It also gives a measured limit: under a constant 100 W load it throttles after about an hour. Other candidates can't be compared side by side, because I found no named-lab measurements for the UGREEN 65W 3-Port, the UGREEN 100W 4-Port wall model, the AOHi The Youth 140W or the Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W. Also, Anker's US page lists the A2688 as Sold Out today. That affects ChatGPT's $69.99 card and our row that says 'See maker page'.
